    AI Overview
    April 20th is primarily known as 4/20, the unofficial international counterculture holiday for celebrating and consuming cannabis. It is also recognized as UN Chinese Language Day, National Look Alike Day, and National Lima Bean Respect Day. 
    Key Details About April 20th: 
    • 4/20 Cannabis Holiday: Enthusiasts often gather at 4:20 p.m. to consume cannabis, with many events focusing on advocating for legalization and reform.
    • Origins: The term originated in the early 1970s with a group of California high schoolers known as the "Waldos".
    • Other Observances:
      • UN Chinese Language Day: Celebrated to promote cultural exchange.
      • National Look Alike Day: A fun day often celebrated by dressing up or acting like someone else.
      • National Lima Bean Respect Day: A quirky food holiday.
    • Cultural Significance: Many cannabis dispensaries offer sales, and major gatherings often occur in cities like San Francisco and Seattle.

    AI Overview
    April 20 is primarily known as the unofficial "420" cannabis culture holiday, celebrating marijuana consumption and advocacy. Originating from a 1970s California high school slang, it has grown into a global day for rallies and industry promotions. Other observations include National Cheddar Fries Day, UN Chinese Language Day, and National Look-Alike Day. 
    Key Details About April 20 
    • 420 Day (Cannabis Culture): Celebrated annually, this day often features large gatherings, protests for legalization, and deals at cannabis dispensaries. It began with a group of teenagers in San Rafael, California, known as the "Waldos," who used "420" as code to meet for smoking
      .
    • National Cheddar Fries Day: Celebrated on April 20 to honor the popular snack.
    • UN Chinese Language Day: Recognized by the United Nations to celebrate the language and its cultural contribution.
    • Other Notable Days: Includes National Look-Alike Day, Lima Bean Respect Day, and National Pineapple Upside-Down Cake Day. 
    In some years, April 20 can coincide with other holidays, such as Easter or Patriot's Day in the U.S..
